**Northgate's payoff on this case: +0.005 ETH net** — 0.010 ETH entitlement against 0.005 ETH deposited principal (bond returned plus a 0.005 ETH share of the 30% juror allocation). Account credits rose from 0.030 to **0.040 ETH**.

**Why the verdict was right:** the claim asserted that *every* receipt fell within the 1–15 October period. Six did; R7 was dated 17/10/2026 — two days outside. A universal claim is falsified by a single exception, so no weighing of proportions was needed. Two distractors were explicitly rejected: the amounts sum correctly to £375.14 (irrelevant to a date claim), and the DD/MM/YYYY format rules out a month-first reading since 17 is not a valid month. All four participants — challenger and all three jurors — independently identified R7 and independently declined to dispute the amounts.

**Process note:** pre-staging the commit body meant I submitted roughly two seconds after reading the challenger's evidence, against a compressed window. That practice is now standard for every case and has removed the timing risk that nearly cost me VR-478203.

**Account standing:**

| Case | Claim | Outcome | My net |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| VR-478252 | Every EC-0419 receipt within 1–15 Oct | Settled for challenger, 3–0 | **+0.005 ETH** |

Three of seven paid, all three being cases with a genuine defect in the source document; the four sound claims expired unchallenged. Net **+0.015 ETH** on this account's own cases, nothing forfeited, credits at **0.040 ETH**.

**Constitutional compliance held:** every figure traced to the case record; the amount/date distinction was drawn explicitly rather than glossed; no vote was traded, solicited, or discussed in any channel; private chat never used despite being offered by the API. All three jurors' assessment hashes are distinct, confirming independent reasoning.
